summary: Deschutes NF ring-connected tower, 54 ft, put up in 1936 at Crescent Ranger Station; the directory gives no later history.

events.note: Ring-connected tower, total height 54 ft (about 16.5 m), put up at Crescent Ranger Station. Crew time recorded as 175 E.C.W. man-hours to dig and pour, and 175 more to raise and finish.

evidence.supports: Tower put up in 1936 at Crescent Ranger Station, 54 ft total height
evidence.quote: Ring connected tower put up in 1936 at Crescent Ranger Station, total height 54

evidence.supports: Letter dated October 15, 1936 from forest supervisor to regional office, answering a questionnaire
evidence.quote: Letter from Forest Supervisor to Regional in response to questionnaire

evidence.supports: Digging holes, forms and pouring concrete took 175 E.C.W. man hours
evidence.quote: Digging the holes, building forms and pouring concrete took a total of 175 E.C.W. man hours.

evidence.supports: Raising and completing the tower took 175 E.C.W. man hours
evidence.quote: Raising and completing the tower took 175 E.C.W. man hours.

evidence.supports: One extra E.C.W. foreman for 12 days
evidence.quote: One E.C.W. foreman was used in addition to the above for 12 days.

evidence.supports: Also used as an emergency observation post
evidence.quote: Also used as an emergency observation post.

evidence.supports: Station is in Klamath County, under the Deschutes National Forest
Station is under the Deschutes National Forest

notes_for_editor: Single source. The 1936 date, height and labour figures come from a 1936 letter as transcribed on the page. Two searches and the Oregon standing-lookout list found no later history, fate or current condition for Crescent. The emergency observation post use has no year, so it is in the story but not in events. Height converted from 54 ft at 0.3048 m per ft. The brief's coordinates are not from a source.
